name: Sparkline
purpose: The axis-free inline trend line — a line chart reduced to pure shape, at two reviewed scales: standalone (with its data table) and inline (the KPI/Stat-card scale, decorative). COMPACT Layer-2 (chart-revisit wave lane ②, 2026-07-24): popover (one focus stop on the trend line) + fit (CSS width release under .dv-fit-on) — deliberately below the exemplar's full set; the spark is ambient. Graduated from the round-one dataviz kit. PROVISIONAL-AGENT: promoted from the PARKED kit (9 review rounds, not signed off).
$provides: s254-D2 item 5 (Dave, #254): chart-sparkline LEAVES the chart-panel role — a brief asking for a panel must never be served an axis-free inline trend. It moves to roles.json `$not-a-provider` as a COMPLEMENT of the headline-metric role (kpi-tile carries the `with` edge). `provides: chart-panel` and `priority: 30` (the values it carried until #254) are REMOVED, not zeroed: a priority with no role is a number about nothing (check 6 priority-in-role). Its own `when`, `answers`, `shape` and `span` stand as authored under s254-D1.
when: answers=change-over-time AND series=1 AND axes=absent AND span.cols ≤ 4 (inline, or a trend cell in a table) — yields to chart-line (88, "change-over-time") whenever the panel can carry axes, and is normally a complement of headline-metric rather than a chart-panel in its own right (ROLES-REVIEW §03).

responsive.rule: preserveAspectRatio:none is SAFE here — a spark contains no text, so DV-D02's text-never-scales is vacuously held (the kit's own exception). FIT (Layer-2): JS-on, .dv-fit-on (dv-behaviour init) releases the standalone's fixed 340px to width:100% — pure CSS aspect stretch, no relayout maths; JS-off = fixed 340 baked (the DV-D02 static answer). Inline stays fixed 200×48.

accessibility.role: Standalone: figure role="group" + sr-only figcaption, svg role="group" with a trend-summary aria-label; the trend polyline = role="img" focus stop. Inline: aria-hidden — decorative; the composed value + period carry the meaning.
accessibility.name: Standalone aria-labels summarise the trend ('rising from 82 to 104'); polyline aria-label == data-tip; the table is the full data surface.
accessibility.keyboard: The trend line is ONE focus stop (tabindex 0 → dvTip popover on focus); the <details> summary is focusable. No per-point stops — receipted (axis-free idiom; the table carries per-month values).
accessibility.nonText: Series stroke ≥3:1 vs the page both modes (dv-016).

antiPatterns: Axis, gridlines or labels on a spark (it is axis-free by definition — that is a line chart)
An inline spark that is NOT aria-hidden (double-announcing decorative shape)
A standalone spark without its table (dv-005 — the shape alone is not data)
Re-typing the Stat-card tile to demo composition (the seam is a Stat-card variant decision — never re-type a sub-atom)

behaviour.fallback: With CSS on and JS off the three standalone canvases render as EMPTY <svg> boxes and no trend line is drawn — dvRender(figure, spec) is what fills them. The data is not lost: every standalone figure carries a real <table class="dv-table"> of its twelve monthly values, authored in the markup and not generated, inside a .dv-tablepanel that is sr-only — no summary, no toggle, no visible surface, because s182-D2 removed the table CTA from this atom and the atom must still look like the graphic and its one tip. So with JS off a screen reader and a text browser both still get the whole series, and a sighted viewer sees the atom's empty footprint rather than a chart that lies. The engine REWRITES those same rows from the spec when it runs, so the popover value and the table value are one number by construction. The INLINE 44px KPI specimen is not engine-drawn and renders in full with JS off — it is aria-hidden and decorative, and the composed tile's value carries the meaning. Lost with JS off: the value popover on the trend line and on the optional min/max dots, and the enclosure re-fit (s184-D1) that re-derives every x from data-fxs on resize.
behaviour.$note: Typed s249-D4 / #259 (the chart-engine sparkline lane). `script` addresses the ENGINE CORE — dv-render.js is the file this component's behaviour begins at; dv-render-sparkline.js is reached through its type registry and is named in `partial`, which is where the registered AUTO-BEHAVIOUR names belong. The member consumes NO dv-legend: a spark is single-series by definition (s182-D2, the atom alone), and the partial throws a named error on a second series rather than drawing a key it has no room for. TWO WORKAROUNDS live inside the type partial rather than in the core, both filed as core requests in notes/_subreports/2026-09-08-259-E-sparkline.md: the partial EMPTIES the core's axis furniture (s182-D2 — the atom is axis-free and the core has no opt-out switch), and it computes its OWN value domain (the core floors every domain at zero for dv-bar-009, which would draw an 82→111 index as a flat smear in the top fifth of the box).
